notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 25-ft bays, W27X146 girders, one 15-ton cab crane, on existing column brackets by others; the rail, girders, ties to the column face, bearings and end stops. Existing building frames, column brackets, anchors and foundations are excluded. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 2.01, flange-tie-flange 1.46 for the estimated tie demands): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.reason: The support reaction, about 245 kN (55 kip), is above the AIST TR-13 §5.9.2 guideline of 222 kN (50 kip) for column brackets, a clause to be verified: consider a crane column tied to the building column or a stepped column; an advisory, not a code limit, so the support entered (Bracket by others (existing)) is kept, by others.

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves saddle-across-fatigue 2.01, flange-tie-flange 1.46 for the estimated tie demands): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.76, vertical deflection 0.26, lateral 0.51 and rail-head movement with twist 0.83 of their limits; flanges at least 267 mm wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 23 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W18X143: tips ratio 0.91 > 0.85; rail-head movement with twist 0.97 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
